$comment: The roadmap board on the roadmap page (landing/roadmap.html, #roadmap). scripts/build-site.mjs renders it into the page.
Edit by hand: areas, their order, and each item's title, description and links (issue and PR numbers of the repo below).
npm run roadmap reads the links' states with gh and rewrites status, release and updated; it keeps everything else.

status: available (merged, and every linked issue closed as completed), development (an open PR, a linked issue with an open PR, part of the work merged, or started: true), planned (open issues only).
release: the first tag that contains the merge commit, e.g. 0.3.0, or next (merged, not released yet; shown as nextRelease).
started: true marks an item whose work has begun before its first PR. Items without links keep the status and release written here.

items.title: Visual designer
items.description: Draw a parametric model, set up the simulation, run it and read the results in one window.

items.title: One-row ribbon
items.description: Home, Modeling, Transform, Simulation, Optimize and Post-processing on one row; the tree, dock and properties collapse, next to a Python side panel.

items.title: Draw in 3D and extrude faces
items.description: Draw a brick's base and then its height in the 3D view, or extrude a picked face into a new part.

items.title: One Transform dialog
items.description: Translate, scale, rotate and mirror in one dialog (Ctrl+T), with a live preview.

items.title: Booleans, polygons included
items.description: Add, subtract and intersect shapes, including polygons, with a colour-coded preview.

items.title: Pick points, align and measure
items.description: Use vertices, edge midpoints and face centres for corners and origins; align parts and measure between points.

items.title: Shortcuts and modeling history
items.description: A sheet of the keyboard shortcuts, and the session's modeling history.

items.title: A tree with context menus
items.description: Right-click menus on every node, show and hide, and drag and drop of parts into components.

items.title: Parameters in the dock
items.description: A table of every parameter next to Checks, with CSV and JSON import and export.

items.title: Checks that explain themselves
items.description: Click a warning to see what was found, why it matters and how to fix it.

items.title: Ports that find their ground
items.description: Add port here says what the port connects to and offers the other metals it found.

items.title: Import VBA macro
items.description: A CST-compatible VBA macro or history list becomes a design, manual mesh lines included, with a report of what was skipped or changed.

items.title: Save As
items.description: Save a design under a new name, in the app and from the File menu; Undo and Redo work from the menus too.

items.title: Checks for misplaced metal
items.description: New warnings for metal that overhangs its substrate or floats off the structure.

items.title: Surface current in the ribbon
items.description: Simulation › Monitors has its own Surface current button, next to Far field.

items.title: Start templates
items.description: A half-wave dipole, a quarter-wave monopole, an open-ended waveguide, a printed sleeve dipole and a two-port microstrip line to start from.

items.title: Import PCB artwork
items.description: DXF, Gerber and Excellon files become a design: Home › Import PCB, or fairbeam import-pcb.

items.title: One-click check fixes
items.description: Common design checks offer a fix you can apply with one click.

items.title: Automatic meshing
items.description: The FDTD mesh is built from the geometry. In the dipole and patch checks, resonance differs from converged hand-tuned meshes by about 0.1% or less.

items.title: Multi-port S-parameters
items.description: Full S-matrices of filters, dividers, couplers and arrays, with Touchstone export.

items.title: Sweeps and optimizer
items.description: Sweep one or two parameters, or let the optimizer tune them towards your goals.

items.title: Metal GPU engine
items.description: An optional Metal build of openEMS on Apple silicon: several times faster, same results.

items.title: CUDA GPU engine
items.description: An optional NVIDIA engine on Windows, in the Run panel: the patch in 2.6 s instead of 53 s.

items.title: Thin copper as sheets
items.description: Realistic 35 µm PCB copper is simulated as sheets, so runs keep a practical time step.

items.title: Convergence checks
items.description: A run that cannot converge is stopped before it starts, with the reason and a fix.

items.title: Thin copper in exported models
items.description: A design exported to Python builds the same copper sheets as the designer's own run.

items.title: Auto mesh mode
items.description: The mesh settings are picked for each design, and any field can be overridden.

items.title: Parameter sweeps
items.description: Sequences over up to six parameters each, checked before they run, queued, and compared run by run.

items.title: A stronger optimizer
items.description: Live progress, the best result kept, any number of parameters, and Bayesian, CMA-ES, particle-swarm, genetic and trust-region searches.

items.title: No run without a port
items.description: A design with no port, or no excited port, is refused with a check instead of failing.

items.title: Examples keep their mesh
items.description: An example opened as a new design keeps its exact mesh lines, so it gives the same results.

items.title: Optimizer skips misplaced metal
items.description: Candidates the design checks refuse are skipped without a simulation and shown as Skipped.

items.title: GPU build by default
items.description: When the GPU build of openEMS is installed, the app starts with it and offers both engines; a general setting switches it.

items.title: Mesh convergence
items.description: Simulation › Mesh convergence… refines the automatic mesh until the results stop changing; fairbeam converge does the same from the command line.

items.title: Run-quality warnings
items.description: A run that did not converge, or whose numbers look suspicious, is flagged in the tree and on its results.

items.title: Far field, currents and beam steering
items.description: 3D patterns, gain and efficiency, surface currents, and array beams steered after the run.

items.title: Drawings, reports and fabrication files
items.description: Dimensioned drawings, publication figures, a PDF report, and Gerber and drill files.

items.title: VBA macro export
items.description: A CST-compatible VBA macro rebuilds the model in the target program.

items.title: Solver times on reference machines
items.description: See how long the same model takes on an Apple M5 Pro and a Ryzen 9 with CUDA.

items.title: Every run kept
items.description: Each run keeps its own result, and Results opens the newest run instead of the preview.

items.title: Results in the design tree
items.description: Each run appears under its design, with its S-parameters, far fields, currents and log.

items.title: Post-processing tab
items.description: Selecting a result opens its plot, compare and export tools in the ribbon.

items.title: Markers
items.description: Resonances, a two-marker bandwidth, hover read-outs and your own markers, with a table.

items.title: Compare runs
items.description: Runs side by side, with the parameters that differ marked; copy or save several runs at once.

items.title: Complex formats and Touchstone
items.description: Copy data and CSV in dB, phase, Re/Im or magnitude/phase, and Touchstone export.

items.title: Result tabs
items.description: Results open as tabs in the main area, with an A/B/C table of the runs.

items.title: Animated surface currents
items.description: Phase-resolved surface currents play as a smooth animation in the 3D view.

items.title: Gain and polarization in patterns
items.description: 3D patterns and cuts in directivity, gain, realized gain, or RHCP and LHCP for circular polarization.

items.title: Far-field card in the 3D view
items.description: Dmax, gain, realized gain, radiation, mismatch and total efficiency and the main lobe, next to the pattern.

items.title: Efficiency result
items.description: 1D Results › Efficiency: mismatch efficiency over the band, with the radiation and total efficiency, per driven port.

items.title: Efficiency over the band
items.description: Optional radiation and total efficiency across the band from Simulation › Monitors › Efficiency, computed after the run without changing the solver time.

items.title: Result summaries
items.description: Headline numbers for each run in the tree and the Runs table, Tables › Summary, and a comparison table of the parameters that differ, to copy or save as CSV.

items.title: 2D field maps with phase and animation
items.description: The Field map tab shows E and H planes as heat maps; Phase and Animate play a time-harmonic animation, in 2D and 3D.

items.title: Desktop app for macOS and Windows
items.description: Installs its own Python and openEMS on first start, for your account, without admin rights.

items.title: Updates in the app
items.description: New versions are offered in the app, checked against their signature, and install themselves.

items.title: Sturdier on Windows
items.description: Proxies are honoured, interrupted downloads resume, and the server always stops with the app.

items.title: Clean updates and uninstall
items.description: On Windows, an update replaces the old files and uninstalling removes the whole folder.

items.title: GPU preference on Windows
items.description: “Prefer the GPU build” on the setup screen now works on Windows too.

items.title: Sharp on scaled displays
items.description: Layouts fit 125 % and 150 % Windows scaling and follow each monitor's pixel density.

items.title: Start, Design and Examples
items.description: Examples open read-only with their results; Open as new design makes an editable copy.

items.title: Native menus and settings
items.description: File, Edit, View, Window and Help menus, an About dialog, general settings and native Save As for exports.

items.title: No lost work
items.description: Closing a project, the window or the app asks to save, discard or cancel when there are unsaved changes.

items.title: A window that fits
items.description: The window opens at a size that fits the screen, or maximized on smaller screens.

items.title: Turkish and English interface
items.description: General settings › Language, native menus included, and a Decimal separator setting.

items.title: Searchable example picker
items.description: Find an example by name, with new 867 MHz collinear and Yagi examples.

items.title: Validated results
items.description: Checked against analytical results.

items.title: Benchmarks on Mac and Windows
items.description: All 14 examples timed on both platforms, with matching results.

items.title: Honest efficiency figures
items.description: Efficiencies above 100 % are flagged, and runs report the end criterion they reached.

items.title: A faster, steadier designer
items.description: The 3D view reuses its geometry, and edits survive slow loads, saves and previews.

items.title: Keyboard access
items.description: Designer commands stay visible and every control can be reached from the keyboard.

items.title: Projects open reliably
items.description: A preview arriving mid-load can no longer replace the project you asked for.

items.title: Faster meshing of detailed designs
items.description: Automatic meshing of polygon designs and arrays runs 4 to 64 times faster.

items.title: A quicker designer
items.description: The Start screen opens in half the time, and checks and saves answer sooner.

items.title: Large designs stay responsive
items.description: Big polygon designs edit, preview and check faster, with identical results.

items.title: Horn efficiency
items.description: Waveguide-port power is calibrated, so the pyramidal horn's radiation efficiency reads about 99 %.
